entry.title: Qwik: Crashing any Qwik Server via Resource thenable
entry.summary:
HIGH · GHSA — npm · score 0.122 · CVE-2026-84994

Affected: @builder.io/qwik, @qwik.dev/core. ### Summary A Qwik server in the default configuration can be crashed with one unauthenticated HTTP request. During qwik-json body parsing, `ResourceSerializer.$fill$` does `Promise.resolve(resource._resolved)`. If `_resolved` is a plain object whose `.then` is a QRL for an unregistered symbol, the async QRL rejects, the rejection is orphaned, and Node terminates the process via its default unhandled-rejection policy. ### Impact One unauthenticated request crashes the server. Looping keeps every replica dead as long as the attacker sends requests.

Affected: github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt. ### Summary Terragrunt's `terragrunt catalog` command clones each repository referenced in your catalog configuration into a temporary working directory. In affected versions, the clone path it derived was deterministic and sat under the shared system temporary directory, in the form `<tmp>/catalog-<base64 sha1 of the repo URL>`. Because that path was predictable and Terragrunt followed a symlink already present there instead of rejecting it, a local attacker could plant a symlink at that path and cause Terragrunt to delete a directory and re-clone into it outside the intended temporary root.
